assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear, original and consequential discovery: the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction at a magic twist angle was followed by experimental observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opening the whole field of moire quantum materials. Impact on materials physics and device-oriented experiments is broad and lasting. As an experimentalist in materials and nanoscale characterization, I value that the effect is controlled by a single tunable structural parameter and is directly visualized by scanning probes and transport.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the theoretical prediction of flat bands (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and the experimental demonstration of correlated and superconducting states (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators). Theory plus experiment gives a natural, fair three-person configuration. Other experimental co-authors and parallel groups exist, and I rely on my own recollection of the detailed credit history rather than independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups worldwide since 2018 across graphene and other moire platforms; the basic picture is stable although the microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated. Roughly eight years from discovery, recognition is timely but the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconducting phase is not settled.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate the experimental record.
Credit among the experimental groups beyond the proposed laureate is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians, from the superfluid-Mott transition to quantum gas microscopes with single-site imaging. The concept of analogue quantum simulation is important, original and has shaped both condensed-matter and AMO physics. The experimental control and imaging are impressive instrumentation achievements.
assessment.attribution: The proposal for Hubbard physics with cold atoms (Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators), the Mott-insulator realization (Greiner, Bloch, Hansch and collaborators) and the quantum gas microscope are distinct contributions; the credited list has four names but only three can be chosen. Proposing Bloch, Greiner and Zoller covers theory and experiment, but excludes Cirac and leaves out co-authors on the original papers, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many laboratories over two decades and now a mainstream platform; the recognition is mature, though it follows prior prizes on cooling and condensation.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the Mott transition experiment, the theoretical proposal, or the microscope.
Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and other contributors is contested.
Overlap with other quantum-simulation candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus tuning-fork sensor made non-contact atomic force microscopy with sub-angstrom oscillation amplitudes and atomic resolution routine, and CO-tip functionalization then resolved the internal bond structure of single molecules. This is a genuine invention that opened new measurements in surface and molecular science. From a microscopy standpoint the discovery or invention criterion is well met and the instrumental clarity is high.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor and demonstrated atomic resolution; Gross, Meyer and colleagues demonstrated sub-molecular resolution with functionalized tips. The three supplied names reflect instrument invention and its decisive application, a plausible configuration. Related AFM and STM lineages (Binnig, Quate, Gerber) are already recognized elsewhere, and credit boundaries with those lineages need care.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted across surface science laboratories and commercial instruments for more than two decades; confirmation is strong and independent. Recognition would be timely, but a possible objection is that the field is regarded as a technique extension of a 1986 prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the earlier scanning-probe prize.
Credit between the sensor invention and the molecular-imaging applications.
Broad physics impact is smaller than for field-defining discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single colour-centre spins such as the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond provided a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale sensor. The work is original, experimentally elegant and has had lasting impact on quantum sensing, magnetometry and imaging at the nanoscale, including biological applications.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Awschalom extended coherent spin control and later work on other defects such as silicon carbide. Lukin is also credited, but I propose these three for the experimental foundation. Allocation among four contributors is not clean and the experimental priority between groups needs scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Replicated and widely extended in many laboratories; applications continue to mature, though some quantum-technology promises are still unrealized.
uncertainties: Who made the decisive first demonstrations of single-spin readout versus later extensions.
Overlap with quantum-information candidates and with Lukin's other credited work.
Whether sensing applications count as a physics discovery or mainly as technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and its generalization to Z2 topological insulators, together with the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a major class of topological matter. The impact on materials physics, spectroscopy and spintronics is lasting and the physical idea is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original Z2 and quantum spin Hall predictions; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang proposing HgTe). The proposed trio is reasonable, but omitting Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes, Moore, Balents, Roy and the ARPES observers makes allocation contentious.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed, including three-dimensional topological insulators by ARPES; more than fifteen years of independent work make it mature.
uncertainties: Strong competing claims from other theorists and from the 3D topological insulator experiments.
Overlap with the other topological-insulator and QAH candidates in the longlist.
Practical applications have lagged the conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record precision, represents a leap in measurement science, enabling tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. The invention is clear and the impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye's group drove the precision to unprecedented levels. A two-person prize is natural. Contributions from other clock groups, and from ion-clock work already recognized, should be considered.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by many national laboratories; recognition could be timely as redefinition of the second approaches, although the field is still advancing quickly.
uncertainties: Precision-measurement prizes were given for optical frequency combs and ion traps, so novelty relative to those must be weighed.
Credit relative to other lattice-clock groups, such as Ye's JILA colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions and the later giant effect in crystalline MgO barriers underpin modern magnetic read heads and MRAM. The importance for technology is high and the thin-film and interface physics is well understood, which suits my interest in interfaces characterized by electron microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki (and Moodera) reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and Yuasa demonstrated giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004, guided by Butler's and Mathon's theory. Moodera and the theorists are not in the selected trio, so the configuration is contentious, and Butler is the one theorist on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and commercially deployed for two decades; a prize would be late rather than premature, but a previous prize (giant magnetoresistance, 2007) covers adjacent territory.
uncertainties: Contested priority among Miyazaki, Moodera and others for the 1995 results.
Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may weigh against it.
Whether the committee treats it as physics rather than device engineering.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire, Kerr-lens mode locking and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors) made ultrafast pulses practical and underpin attosecond science, frequency combs and time-resolved spectroscopy, including the experiments recognized in 2023. Lasting enabling impact and clear inventions.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed Ti:sapphire as a gain medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking, and Keller invented SESAM mode locking. These are distinct inventions and the proposed trio is plausible, though others in the Kerr-lens story could argue for credit.
assessment.maturity: Entirely mature, with decades of use; the issue is whether the contribution is now considered an enabling tool whose recognition is long overdue, or whether it falls between prior ultrafast-laser prizes.
uncertainties: Proximity to prior prizes in ultrafast and frequency-comb physics.
Attribution among Kerr-lens mode-locking contributors is not certain from supplied information.
I am relying on memory of the invention history and have not verified the dates.
